results.strategy_description: The Lynx Program is our original strategy that was launched in May 2000. The objective of the Lynx Program is to generate a high risk-adjusted return while maintaining attractive portfolio characteristics. The characteristics have been chosen with the aim of making the strategy suitable as a building block in an institutional investor's portfolio. Examples of these characteristics include a low correlation to equities and bonds, a positive correlation to volatility and positive skewness of returns. Other characteristics relate to the ability to react to trend reversals and profit from prolonged bear market conditions (often referred to as "crisis alpha"). The Lynx Program's main approach is systematic advanced trend following. The program is employing a multi-model approach applying a range of statistical techniques to identify and capture trends over a span of time frames. In addition to trend following concepts, the strategy includes an allocation to diversifying models that aim to exploit other market phenomena than price momentum. These diversifying models consists of systematic global macro concepts based on fundamental data as well as models utilizing various machine learning techniques. In total the program consists of approximately 40 different models. The Investment Committee is responsible for strategy including setting the risk allocation to each model in the program.

results.strategy_description:
Overview
Global Opportunities (GO) is Goldman Sachs Asset Management’s flagship, direct global multi-strategy hedge fund. It invests across global fixed income, equity, commodity, currency and volatility markets, through discretionary and quantitative (roughly 60 / 40% split), relative value and macro (roughly 55% / 45% split) alpha strategies.  The fund combines 38 existing alpha engines from across Goldman Sachs Asset Management’s public investing business to deliver our highest conviction strategies. The strategy leverages existing people, data, technology, infrastructure, and the full resources of the business and firm, to deliver returns consistent with the multi-strategy hedge fund universe, but in more investor focused terms. The fund does not have pass-through fees, and offers monthly liquidity with no lock up on capital.  The solution is designed  to deliver a high Sharpe, low beta to risk assets (~0.0-0.1), cash +7 to 10% net  returns, and 5% to  8% annualized volatility.

The fund is managed by co-CIOs Dennis Walsh and Simon Dangor.  Dennis is also co-CIO of our Quantitative Investment Solutions business and Simon is deputy CIO of Fixed income and head of Global Fixed Income Macro Strategies.

results.management_company_description:
Crabel is a global alternative investment firm specializing in systematic, automated trading of worldwide futures and foreign exchange. Our Los Angeles based firm was founded by short-term trading pioneer Toby Crabel and has delivered over 30 years of uncorrelated returns for its institutional clients. The firm has developed a diverse array of trading strategies designed to systematically capture market anomalies implemented through a technologically advanced, low latency infrastructure. Global co-location facilities and proprietary execution algorithms allow the firm to efficiently trade in approximately 200 futures and foreign exchange markets.

* Firm/Fund Information as of: March 1, 2024
results.strategy_description:
Crabel Gemini is a systematic portfolio of predominantly short holding period strategies designed to target behavioral and structural market inefficiencies across a broadly diversified set of global futures and foreign exchange instruments. The portfolio is structured to provide low correlation to traditional and alternative asset classes. Made up of over 50 differentiated and stand-alone strategy frameworks, the program offers a unique source of returns. Crabel’s focus on execution excellence provides a further advantage in efficiently accessing unique exposures in approximately 200 markets. Strategies are generally driven by price or derivatives of price such as volatility, correlation and term structure. Most strategies are designed to work symmetrically, either long or short. The program has an approximate eight-day average hold timeframe (with a range of two days to several months) and targets a 10% annualized standard deviation. The program utilizes a multi-tiered approach to risk control that includes dynamic sizing of new trades relative to market volatility, the use of price as well as time-based stops and a real-time VaR-based position sizing mechanism that seeks to constrain overall portfolio risk.



Fund Inception refers to inception of the Crabel Gemini program as a distinct trading program.

Fund AUM/Strategy Level AUM represents direct fund assets (adjusted by the applicable leverage factor for Crabel Gemini) and managed account assets including notional equity.

results.name: Samlyn Portable Alpha Fund
results.management_company_description: Samlyn Capital, LLC (the “Firm”), is a global asset management company that manages a Delaware limited partnership and two Cayman Islands exempted companies in a mini-master fund structure that employ a long/short equity strategy (collectively, the “Flagship Fund”), a traditional master-feeder fund structure that employs a long only equity strategy (the “Long Alpha Fund”), a traditional master-feeder fund structure that employs a market-neutral investment strategy (the “Net Neutral Fund”) and a portable alpha investment strategy that invests its assets in shares of a Net Neutral Fund and shares of an exchange-traded fund (the “Portable Alpha Fund” and collectively, the “Funds”).
results.strategy_description:
The Portable Alpha Fund's investment objective is to generate superior risk-adjusted returns over time. In seeking to achieve this objective, the Portable Alpha Fund invests approximately: (i) 50% of the Fund’s net assets in common shares of Samlyn Net Neutral Master Fund, Ltd. (the “Net Neutral Fund”); and (ii) 50% of the Fund’s net assets in shares of the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (ticker: VOO), as well as options thereon (such ratio, the “Target Ratio”). Samlyn rebalances the Fund’s portfolio as of the end of any month in which the Fund’s portfolio has deviated from the Target Ratio by more than 5% as a result of the relative performance of the Fund’s investment in the Net Neutral Fund vis-à-vis the Fund’s investment in shares of the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF and its other direct investments.
Upon the request of a prospective investor, the Fund may in the future establish a new sub-class of shares that invests in a different ETF (in lieu of investing in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF) and maintains a different Target Ratio.

The Net Neutral Fund's investment objective is to generate superior risk-adjusted returns over time by employing a market-neutral investment strategy that makes long and short investments primarily in global equity securities. In particular, the Net Neutral Fund’s portfolio generally mirrors both the long and short positions held by the long/short strategy. However, as the Net Neutral Fund’s portfolio is managed to be market-neutral, the positions held by the Net Neutral Fund are weighted differently than the same positions held in the respective portfolios of the long/short strategy to: (i) neutralize the Net Neutral Fund’s net exposure; and (ii) achieve higher gross exposure for the Net Neutral Fund through the use of increased leverage. The Net Neutral Fund’s gross exposure typically ranges from 300% to 400%. The Net Neutral Fund maintains short basket hedges that are typically adjusted by the Investment Manager on a daily basis in order to neutralize net exposure resulting from daily trading activity and market movements. Short basket hedges may also be used in order to mitigate certain sector and factor exposures, as well as to address macro risks, in each case, as the Investment Manager determines to be appropriate in its discretion. The short basket hedge will also be used to offset net exposure resulting from pair-trades and merger-arbitrage transactions. The Net Neutral Fund’s short basket hedges will consist of broad-based stock indices, sector indices and factor baskets and will generally not exceed 15% of the Net Neutral Fund’s equity. The Net Neutral Fund’s long and short ratios will generally be maintained as long as the Net Neutral Fund’s total gross exposure is typically between 300% to 400% of equity and the short basket hedge exposure is typically between 5% to 15% of equity.

A Portable Alpha Fund investor’s ability to redeem its shares attributable to a particular subscription in the Portable Alpha Fund will be subject to all of the applicable redemption terms set forth in the Samlyn Net Neutral CEM. A summary of the Net Neutral Fund Terms can be found in the Net Neutral Fund CEM (available upon request).

results.strategy_description:

The Fund aims to deliver attractive and consistent returns while minimizing the risk of loss. Our absolute-return strategy seeks to: generate positive returns in every market environment, minimize downside risk, and add diversification in multi-asset portfolios by maintaining the following attributes:
 
Equity-like returns: Our strategy seeks to be capital efficient, moving enough that it delivers meaningful diversification benefits but not so much that it introduces unwanted volatility.
 
Low correlation to stock and bond markets: The Fund is designed to be a source of alpha that’s uncorrelated with major beta drivers in an effort to help our investors achieve better overall performance.
 
Minimal drawdowns: The Fund seeks to maintain a large number of uncorrelated and positively convex positions with upside potential that we believe exceeds their perceived risk of loss. This feature aims to keep the depth and duration of drawdowns to a minimum.

The Fund is an absolute-return strategy that seeks to deliver superior risk-adjusted returns in up or down markets. Cynosure’s systematic approach in managing the Fund combines three uncorrelated models that aim to make performance more consistent, explainable, targeted, and predictable.  

We believe that layering uncorrelated models provides the potential to boost risk-adjusted returns relative to a single-model-driven strategy. Cynosure may adjust the models over time consistent with its model management procedures. Cynosure retains discretion to determine the timing and manner of executing on trading recommendations from the quantitative models and whether to override such recommendations.

*There is no assurance that any of the three models, either individually or in the aggregate, will be successful or will result in positive returns. The expected attribution of performance to each model’s strategy is based on Cynosure’s assessment as of the date of this summary but may change over time. The Fund may acquire investments subject to existing financing or may obtain new financing and may incur secured or unsecured indebtedness at the asset level and/or the Fund level, subject to any restrictions set forth in the Fund’s governing documents. In addition to other forms of leverage, including investments in derivative instruments that are inherently leveraged, the Fund may borrow funds in order to be able to make additional investments, and the Fund may borrow funds in order to cover its expenses or pay redemptions. The use of leverage can, in certain circumstances, maximize the losses to which the Fund’s portfolio of investments may be subject, and the amount of leverage that the Fund may have outstanding at any time may be significant in relation to its assets. Any event that adversely affects the value of an investment would be magnified to the extent that the Fund is leveraged. The cumulative effect of the use of leverage by the Fund in a market that moves adversely to the Fund’s portfolio of investments could result in a substantial loss to the Fund, which would be greater than if the Fund were not leveraged. The access to capital could be impaired by many factors, including market forces or regulatory changes. results.strategy_description: The Brigade Leveraged Capital Structures Fund (the “LCS Fund”) is a long/short credit fund investing throughout the capital structures of U.S. and international leveraged companies. Its primary strategies include L/S corporate credit, distressed, corporate structured credit, and L/S leveraged equities. The Fund's investment universe includes companies with debt or debt-like obligations rated below investment grade, or securities trading at yields comparable to the high yield market. The Fund seeks long-term growth of capital independent of the specific market environment while emphasizing the preservation of capital. Brigade generally utilizes a bottom-up, fundamental research-based process which focuses on free cash flow generation and asset coverage to uncover opportunities.

results.strategy_description: This is a European long/short corporate credit strategy with an opportunistic and often catalyst-driven approach, founded in 2009 by Barend Pennings. It uses bottom-up fundamental credit analysis, focusing on single name corporate issues. We believe the strategy has a particular edge in European high-yield credit situations, where the competitive field is reduced. The strategy has flexibility to invest across geographic jurisdictions, industries, capital structures, and instruments. It has limited net exposure (typically ~50% to ~75%) to reduce correlation with both credit and equity market indices, with a medium- to long-term investment horizon of 6-24 months. Returns are weighted towards capital gains, rather than carry.

results.strategy_description:
TT Emerging Markets Macro Fund (launched April 2025) targets low-to-mid-teens % returns with 6–8% volatility. It is a discretionary, top-down EM macro strategy focused on localised opportunities across FX, rates, and credit. It is differentiated by its proprietary models which exploit mispricing created by the dominance of local EM investors in a de-globalised world, offering diversification away from both benchmark constraints and developed-market bias.

The fund offers a return profile uncorrelated to traditional EM long-only strategies, with performance driven by idiosyncratic macro themes rather than broad market direction. It is designed to thrive in environments where traditional correlations across sub-asset-classes evolve or break down, and seeks to capture risk asymmetries arising from differing perceptions of risk among economic agents. This is underpinned by a deep understanding of local macro drivers & flow dynamics, regulatory frameworks, and the exploration of repressed or underpriced scenarios.

results.management_company_description:
Senator Investment Group LP (“Senator” or the “Firm”) is a private investment firm co-founded in 2008 by Douglas Silverman to pursue investments opportunistically across the capital structure with an emphasis on identifying companies undergoing change. The Firm manages the Senator Global Opportunity Funds ("SGOF", or, the "Funds"), its flagship event-driven hedge fund launched in July 2008. SGOF employs a fundamental investment approach identifying catalyst-driven equities and dislocated or otherwise attractive credit instruments, while being cognizant and thoughtful of macro factors. The Funds invest globally, with the majority of exposures in the U.S. and an average historical net long exposure between 30%-60%. Senator has managed several other funds, strategies, and accounts during its 18 year history. The Firm is also currently accepting outside capital for the Senator Strategic Resources Fund ("SSRF"), a long-biased, thematic equity fund initially funded with internal capital in 2023.  SSRF seeks to capitalize on companies, commodities, and currencies that are at the confluence of global megatrends including Fiscal Dominance, Deglobalization, and Societal Transformation.  

Senator is based in New York City and has 27 employees, of whom 13 are investment professionals. The Firm's analysts are ambidextrous with respect to both credit and equity investing. Senator believes this flexibility and breadth of expertise has enabled the Firm to pursue attractive risk returns throughout market cycles.
results.strategy_description: The Senator Global Opportunity Fund was formed in July 2008 to pursue opportunistic investments, long and short, in distressed and dislocated credit and catalyst-driven equities. The Fund will invest opportunistically across the capital structure wherever it identifies the best risk-reward, driven by a fundamentals first investment process and informed by its macro and risk framework; therefore the Fund may have a distinct bias toward equity or credit at different points in the cycle. Senator employs an “event-driven” framework in its investment process. However, unlike many event-driven funds where the “event” often leads the analysis and/or idea generation, Senator’s investment strategy is foremost rooted in identifying companies with strong fundamentals (although potentially in distress) at attractive valuations, and that may benefit from a corporate event or catalyst over a 6 – 18 month period.  Senator employs a bottom-up approach to analyzing all components of a company's capital structure and invests in a broad range of securities including bank debt, corporate bonds, equities, preferred stock, convertible securities, trade claims, credit default swaps, and options. Senator emphasizes capital preservation and seeks to mitigate risk through various hedging strategies at the position and portfolio levels. Senator also monitors a number of macro and risk factors to ensure the portfolio’s intended bets are expressed and unintended bets managed. These factors include, but are not limited to, concentration, sector, market cap, region, liquidity, crowdedness, momentum, and ESG scores. Net exposure levels have averaged ~40% since inception.

results.strategy_description: Bayberry Capital Partners (“Bayberry”) was founded in 2019 by Angela Aldrich and Brian Smith, who worked together at John Griffin's Blue Ridge Capital for over six years.  Bayberry is a global, concentrated, fundamental primary research-driven long / short equity fund. Our objective is to generate positive, idiosyncratic, and largely uncorrelated absolute returns for our investors, driven by security selection, deep fundamental primary research, discipline throughout the lifecycle of each individual investment, and a relentless focus on protecting and compounding investor capital irrespective of market environment.  The idea generation and research processes focus on largely undiscovered idiosyncratic small- and mid-cap opportunities globally and across sectors and seek to offer investors access to a portfolio of names to which they are un- or at least under-exposed. Bayberry optimizes for opportunities where we believe the team’s deep, creative, and fundamental research process can provide a competitive advantage, and underwrite investments to a 3–5-year holding period, focusing on attractive long-term opportunities.  Short-selling is a core focus rather than an afterthought, and the fund aims to generate absolute return on both sides of the portfolio – short alpha since inception is greater than +90% versus the SPX.  Our portfolio is a product of creative idea generation, extensive primary research, focused portfolio optimization, and prudent risk management.

Equity Securities.  The Fund may invest in equity securities and equity-related securities.  The value of these financial instruments generally will vary with the performance of the issuer and movements in the equity markets.  In addition, equity securities that Bayberry believes are undervalued or incorrectly valued may not ultimately be valued by the markets in the manner that Bayberry anticipates.  As a result, the Fund may suffer losses if it invests in equity instruments of issuers whose performance diverges from Bayberry’s expectations or if equity markets generally move in a single direction and the Fund has not hedged against such a general move. 
Hedging Transactions.  Bayberry may engage in certain hedging transactions, including derivatives, options, and swaps. Hedges can be more difficult to implement than many other types of transactions, and the possibilities for errors may be greater than for other transactions.  While the Fund may enter into hedging transactions to seek to reduce risk, such transactions may result in a poorer overall performance for the Fund than if it had not engaged in such hedging transactions.  The success of Bayberry’s hedging strategy is subject to Bayberry’s ability to correctly assess the degree of correlation between the performance of the instruments used in the hedging strategy and the performance of the investments in the portfolios being hedged. Since the characteristics of many securities change as markets change or time passes, the success of the instances when Bayberry hedges portfolio positions in the Fund is also subject to Bayberry’s ability to continually recalculate, readjust, and execute hedges in an efficient and timely manner. 
Short Selling.  Bayberry may engage in short selling on behalf of the Fund.  Short selling involves selling securities that are not owned by the Fund.  A short position is established when the Fund borrows securities from securities brokers or other institutions and sells them in an open market transaction with an obligation to return the borrowed securities at a later date.  However, a short sale creates the risk of unlimited loss because in order to close out a short position, the Fund would need to return the borrowed securities by purchasing such securities at prevailing market prices.  There can be no assurance that the security necessary to close out a short position will be available for purchase.  Purchasing securities to close out the short position can itself cause the price of the securities to rise further if the demand to buy such securities outpaces the available supply, thereby exacerbating the loss.

results.management_company_description:
Founded in 1971 and based in Los Angeles, TCW manages a broad range of innovative, actively managed investment products that strive to enhance and protect clients’ wealth. TCW’s clients include many of the largest corporate and public pension plans, financial institutions, insurance companies, endowments and foundations in the United States, as well as a substantial number of international entities including central banks, sovereign wealth funds and private banks.

In 2001, TCW was acquired by Société Générale (SG), one of the largest global banking franchises with a presence in 85 countries. SG worked with TCW to grow and expand its global footprint for a dozen years. The partnership was very productive, including in early 2010, TCW’s acquisition of Metropolitan West Asset Management, LLC (MetWest), a top-ranked fixed income asset manager. As a result, key employees of MetWest assumed primary responsibility for the oversight of TCW’s fixed income mandates. Since that time, MetWest has operated as a subsidiary of The TCW Group, Inc. 

In February 2013, TCW’s management effected a management led buy-out of SG in partnership with The Carlyle Group. Following the buyout, The Carlyle Group held an approximately 60% stake in the firm, with TCW management and employees owning the balance of approximately 40%, on a fully diluted basis. TCW management negotiated strong governance provisions to ensure that TCW’s managerial autonomy would be preserved. Equity for the transaction came from TCW management and two Carlyle investment funds – Carlyle Global Financial Services Partners, a $1.1 billion financial services fund, and Carlyle Partners V, a $13.7 billion U.S. buyout fund. The Carlyle transaction facilitated a management initiative to increase employee ownership.  Prior to 2010, TCW employees did not have significant equity interests in the firm. Since the 2010 acquisition of MetWest by TCW, employee ownership has continued to increase.

On December 27, 2017, Nippon Life completed its acquisition of a 24.75% minority stake in TCW from Carlyle. As a result of this transaction, ownership in TCW by TCW management and employees increased to 44.07%, and Carlyle maintains a 31.18% interest in the firm through a purchase by its long duration private equity fund, Carlyle Global Partners.

There is a high level of employee ownership of the company, including most of TCW’s key decision-making investment and other professionals. TCW believes strongly that employee equity ownership aligns the interests of the decision-making employees with the interests of the firm and the firm’s clients, and creates a cohesive “ownership culture.”

Nippon and Carlyle have agreed to continue the existing strong governance protections for TCW management, which help to ensure that TCW’s current management and investment teams are primarily responsible for personnel and compensation decisions, and solely responsible for the management of investment portfolios.
results.strategy_description:
The investment team employs a fundamental research-driven and value-oriented approach as it seeks to to identify opportunities in the small cap equity markets. The team strives to distinguish market mispricings that may result from a transitional event, a complex corporate restructure, and lack of research coverage or institutional investor focus.

The team actively seeks out companies that are in transition and therefore, more likely to be under or overvalued by the market. Once an opportunity is recognized, the team performs a deep dive to determine the fundamental value of the company. While analyzing the single security, our selection process incorporates the overall portfolio impact by managing risk through extensive bottom-up research, active hedging, reassessing portfolio construction, and exposure monitoring.

We believe changes in regulation and the shift to passive indexing in the equity market should result in more opportunities since there should be less capital and fewer institutional investors following off-the-run names. We assert that these shifts are likely to result in larger differences between intrinsic and market value when a company is in transition.

Portfolio Manager, Jeremy Zhu established the strategy in 2003 and has managed the fund since inception. Each member of the team has over 15 years of investment experience and have been investing together the past decade. While they have different areas of expertise, they share the same investment philosophy.

results.strategy_description:
The Arrow Market Neutral Fund is an Australian domiciled wholesale unit trust. The fund is offered to sophisticated and wholesale investors in Australia and New Zealand. International investors can access the strategy via the Arrow Mercury (Cayman) Fund, which is managed as a 2X levered version of the core strategy. The Manager also offers the strategy to institutional investors via separately managed accounts.

The Fund employs a global equity market neutral strategy constructing long and short portfolios of roughly the same value and characteristics. The Manager selects securities from a universe comprising 4 key geographies - Australia Hong Kong Japan and the United States restricting itself to large liquid securities only. Using a thematic approach the Manager seeks to identify structural and cyclical themes which it believes will have a material impact on the price of certain securities. Having identified and validated a theme the Manager builds baskets of 5-20 securities which it believes have a meaningful exposure to the theme. Through bottom-up fundamental analysis the Manager curates each basket to identify high quality companies which it believes are positively exposed to the theme and poor quality companies that are negatively exposed to the theme. Thematic baskets are managed dynamically to ensure the theme as a whole along with each constituent security is performing in line with the Manager's expectations.

The Manager has a strict risk management framework which requires that the net equity exposure of the portfolio (cash & beta adjusted) is kept at or close to zero at all times. Each geographic block is also kept neutral at all times to ensure FX or other regional factors are neutralized. The Manager constructs broadly diversified long and short portfolios with the Fund typically holding 150-180 individual positions (skewed higher to shorts). Liquidity is also a key consideration with constant monitoring to ensure that a high liquidity hurdle is retained for all investments. This allows the Manager to control drawdowns by cutting losing positions quickly.

Virtual Currency Derivatives: The Investment Manager may purchase and sell virtual currency derivatives (i.e., futures and options). These instruments
have some unique features and risks, including, but not limited to those described in this paragraph. Virtual currency futures trading commenced on
exchanges in the United States in December 2017. Therefore, there is a limited price history for these contracts which the Investment Manager may
use as inputs into its trading signals. There is no significant fundamental market supply and demand affecting virtual currency futures. Rather, the
underlying spot market is predominantly composed of speculators. The prices of the virtual currencies which underlie these futures contracts are
extremely volatile (i.e. certain virtual currencies have experienced daily price volatility of more than 20%). Virtual currency derivatives may experience
significant price volatility. The rules of certain designated contract markets impose trading halts that may restrict the ability of the Investment Manager
to exit a position during a period of high volatility. The difficulty in valuing the underlying virtual assets can in turn pose significant challenges in reliably
valuing virtual asset futures contracts. The initial margin for virtual currency derivatives may be set as a percentage of the value of a particular contract,
which means that margin requirements for long positions can increase if the price of the contract rises. Some clearing brokers may pose restrictions on
customer trading activity in virtual currency derivatives, such as requiring additional margin, imposing position limits, prohibiting naked shorting or
prohibiting give-in transactions. In addition, some clearing brokers currently do not permit their customers to trade in virtual currency derivatives or only
allow certain customers to trade virtual currency derivatives. If the clearing broker were to impose restrictions on or prohibit the Fund from trading virtual
currency derivatives, the Fund could incur significant losses. The rules of certain exchanges impose trading halts that may restrict a market participant's
ability to exit a position during a period of high volatility. The underlying "cash" markets for virtual currency derivatives are largely unregulated or
supervised by a government agency. Because of this the virtual currency derivatives markets may be unusually susceptible to fraud and manipulation,
which could adversely affect the price of virtual currency derivatives. Regulators from various (major) jurisdictions have been scrutinizing virtual
currencies and virtual currency derivatives for example by imposing requirements, restrictions or a total ban on the sale of or trading in virtual currency
futures. All these risks and features could result in regulatory burdens, high costs, a low degree of efficiency when trading and ultimately substantial
losses.

Newly Developed Contracts: The Investment Manager may trade newly developed contracts, including without limitation, Bitcoin and Ethereum futures
contracts, mini-futures and options thereon and such other cryptocurrency futures contracts which may become listed for trading on futures exchanges
from time to time. In the United States, designated contract markets self-certify new futures contracts following consultation with the CFTC. Likewise,
foreign regulatory authorities are typically required to authorize the trading of new futures contracts on exchanges within their countries. Periodically,
designated contract markets may self-certify new futures contracts and options and foreign regulatory authorities may designate additional contracts as
approved contracts. If the Investment Manager determines that it is appropriate to trade in a new contract, it may do so on behalf of the Fund’s account.
Because these contracts are new, the Investment Manager’s trading strategies may not be applicable to, or advisable for, these contracts. The markets
in new contracts, moreover, have been historically both illiquid and highly volatile for some period of time after the contract begins trading. These
contracts therefore present significant risk potential.

results.strategy_description: Decagon Asset Management ("DAM")  employs a hard-catalyst event-driven strategy, investing globally and across the capital structure, focused on announced corporate events. The Strategy is agnostic to geography, sector and instrument and seeks to achieve attractive risk-adjusted returns with low volatility. The Strategy is intended to be market neutral and uncorrelated to any other asset class. The Strategy primarily invests in equities but can also express risk arbitrage investments via listed credit instruments, although these investments are limited in order to maintain the Strategy's desired liquidity profile. Investments are driven by bottom-up fundamental research and a top-down data driven analysis, seeking to benefit from market dislocations and inefficiencies. The Strategy typically holds 20-30 long positions (or long spreads) and 0-5 short positions (or short spreads). The Strategy aims to manage to a maximum estimated loss of 3% of AUM per position, a maximum position size of 15% of LMV, and maximum gross leverage of 320%. The Firm aims to manage the portfolio with limited leverage in tight or normal markets in order to be in a position of strength during periods of market dislocation. We believe this gives us the ability to increase our exposure and invest in opportunities that we believe to be mispriced. Risk LMV target of 80-120% in tight or normal markets and up to 200% in times of dislocation. The Strategy aims to have minimal market beta and utilises a convex portfolio hedge to help achieve this goal. The Fund aims to be highly liquid so that 90% of the portfolio could be liquidated within two weeks under normal market conditions.

results.name: Sternlight Credit Opportunities Fund
results.management_company_description:
Sternlight generates alpha through a repeatable process targeting asymmetric, catalyst-driven long and short opportunities in European credit. The strategy is run by a team with decades of fundamental investment experience and is well positioned to capitalize on the growing market dislocations across the liquid European credit universe.  

The team is led by Stefan Tsonev (CIO) who has over 27 years of investment experience, most recently as a senior portfolio manager for the flagship, multi-billion dollar credit hedge funds at PIMCO, in London.

The Firm began deploying the strategy in September 2023 in a managed account format - if interested, please get in touch and we would be happy to discuss the strategy and returns.
results.strategy_description:
The Sternlight Credit Opportunities Fund Limited launched in June 2025 with $200M of seed capital from an institutional investor.  A Founders' class is available for the next $200M of investments with discounted fees.  
The Fund will be deploying a strategy which has a track record (available on request) covering the period from inception of the strategy in September 2023 to date.
The strategy's objectives are to generate double-digit returns, with low volatility over a full cycle, together with a low correlation to high yield credit and equity beta.

results.name: Oceanic Hedge Fund
results.management_company_description:
Oceanic Investment Management Ltd. (OIM) has been established for more than thirty years as a financial investment and advisory group specialising in the maritime and energy sectors. Oceanic Hedge Fund (OHF) commenced in August 2002.
 
Fund activity has also featured several managed accounts with related strategies.
results.strategy_description:
OHF invests in the Shipping and Energy sectors, through long/short equity, bonds, commodities and freight. The investment process comprises a short-term trading strategy and a medium-term fundamental strategy. 

The short-term strategy utilities a proprietary vessel tracking and prediction software, “TRACS”, which provides real-time tracking of all ships on the water.  The fundamental analysis draws on a 150 year shipping market database, extensive in-house demand/supply analyses and stock specific asset valuations. The strategy also seeks to capture structural opportunities arising from the energy transition and applies operational and technical analysis to identify the winners and losers from increasingly stringent environmental standards.
